存储这块我一直是看多的，不过AI链条里最舒服的位置其实不在韩国，在日本。

HBM 说到底就是把十几层die磨薄、切开、叠起来，再一层一层测过去。磨片和切割机基本是Disco一家的生意，测试机全世界就爱德万和泰瑞达两家在分。HBM 一颗的测试时间是普通DRAM的好几倍，层数从8往12、16堆，测试时间还在往上涨。良率差、返工多的那些批次，机器占用的时间更长。爱德万的钱是按机时收的。

三星、海力士、美光在那边拼产能、拼良率，这几家日本公司每多叠一层就多抽一道，谁家先爬上去其实不太影响他们的账。

日经爬回1989年那个高点花了三十四年。最后这段路上出力的，有一部分在首尔。

text:
【美股复盘 · 10月19日】

**大市**

美股周一(10月19日)三大指数表现分歧，资金明显由旧经济向科网股一边倾斜。纳指 
$QQQ
 高开高走，全日收报718.36点，升1.21%，为主要指数中表现最强；标普500 SPY 收报766.48点，升0.42%；道指 DIA 则反复偏软，收报518.92点，微跌0.03%，是唯一失守平盘的主要指数；罗素小型股 IWM 收报271.29点，升0.31%。市宽温和偏好，104只观察股中64只上升、40只下跌。反向ETF同步急泻，做空纳指的 SQQQ 挫3.55%，做空半导体的 SOXS 重挫5.28%，侧面印证科技及芯片板块的买盘力度。

**板块**

存储及半导体链一枝独秀。 WDC 暴升6.09%， SNDK 急升5.53%，同属存储阵营；半导体测试设备股 AEHR 升4.50%， MRVL 升4.06%， SMTC 升4.02%。外围连动，韩股ETF EWY 升4.08%， SKHY 升4.67%，与存储周期的强势互为呼应。大型科网方面， AMZN 升4.98%，为权重股中升幅最显著者， PLTR 升4.36%。

沽压则集中于金融与旧经济。银行股领跌大市， JPM 跌1.82%， BAC 跌1.64%；汽车股同受压， F 跌2.01%， GM 跌1.44%。加密资产相关股份反复转弱， COIN 挫2.72%， HOOD 跌2.38%。药股分化， MRK 跌1.59%，惟 MRNA 逆市造好，升4.07%。量子计算概念股 IONQ 跌1.60%。

**焦点**

题材面上，市场对半导体人才结构的讨论升温。业内数据显示，英伟达的员工离职率已降至约1%，为全行业最低；分析指这与未行使RSU的留任成本直接相关，而非单纯的文化因素。半导体业的历史本身就是一部出走史——仙童半导体当年流出的人才直接催生Intel与AMD，后续衍生数十家公司，黄仁勋本人亦出身LSI Logic。离职率压至极低，意味着这条传统的新公司孵化链条在当前周期内明显收窄。

苹果方面，据报道将于10月28日的发布会推出首款触控屏MacBook。市场关注点多在交互形态的转向，惟真正牵动账本的是抽成结构：iPad Pro用户群软件分发只能走App Store，佣金不漏；macOS则容许开发者自行分销，产品线的边界如何划定，关系到软件服务收入的税基。另一方面，特斯拉与SpaceX的合并传闻持续，当中的换股比例为关键——马斯克于SpaceX的持股比例远高于特斯拉，若以特斯拉发行新股换取SpaceX股权，摊薄成本由特斯拉现有股东承担。

**小结**

全日格局为典型的板块轮动而非全面上扬：存储、半导体与大型科网承托指数，金融、汽车及加密相关股份则持续受压，道指因权重偏重旧经济而未能跟上。市宽64升40跌，升幅谈不上一致，反向ETF的双位数级别跌幅则显示空仓在芯片一端被压得较紧。分析指，后市须留意存储链的升势能否扩散至更广的半导体板块，以及银行股的沽压是否属轮动的一体两面；若金融与科网的分歧继续扩大，指数层面的升幅仍将高度依赖少数权重股。

The selloff continues. Next, I’m shifting from shorting beta to shorting alpha. I call it the “reverse bottleneck trade”—the counterpart to the earlier bottleneck trade.

The logic is simple: AI demand will keep growing, but that growth may slow, while upstream suppliers keep expanding capacity in response to shortages and fat margins. Once effective supply catches up with demand, bargaining power shifts back downstream. During a shortage, customers care first about availability. Good enough will do. Once supply is plentiful, they start comparing performance, cost, power consumption, and reliability again. That’s when we find out who wins orders on competitiveness and who was simply picking up overflow because the leaders couldn’t supply enough.

My watchlist includes memory runner-up MU, second- and third-tier optical players COHR and AAOI, and foundry runner-up INTC.

This trade doesn’t even require the AI bubble to burst. Supply growth just needs to start outpacing demand growth. I think there’s a very high probability these stocks put in an “Everest chart” over the next year—a towering peak followed by a collapse back down. If you don’t have the stomach to go all-in on outright shorts, anti-bottleneck pair trades are another good way to express the view: long LITE / short AAOI; long TSM / short INTC; long NVDA / short AMD or AVGO.

As I've said before, technological diffusion is an irreversible process, and China has consistently outpaced the US when it comes to driving down costs. The technological moat enjoyed by closed-source frontier AI labs simply cannot last forever.

The latest release of DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash-1017 is yet another reminder of this reality. With only 8B–16B activated parameters, the model reportedly achieved a 77% Pass@1 score on DeepSWE v1.1, outperforming several leading proprietary models on this particular benchmark at a fraction of the cost.

This is a fundamental shift. Open-source models are no longer just "good enough" alternatives to proprietary models. They are increasingly capable of matching—and potentially surpassing—the most advanced closed-source models in specific domains, while dramatically undercutting their economics.

And this process is only accelerating.

Eventually, we'll see highly capable AI models running on a single RTX 5090, or even an ordinary laptop. As intelligence becomes increasingly commoditized and the cost of inference continues to collapse, the scarcity premium embedded in today's AI valuations will become harder and harder to justify.

At that point, continuing to trade the so-called "bottleneck" narrative as if compute scarcity were a permanent structural advantage would be absurd.

The AI trade as we know it is coming to an end.

This is a really interesting chart.
I attended the TrendForce San Francisco roadshow yesterday, and this chart got me thinking about a lot of things.

China is now expected to localize more than half, or close to half, of most equipment categories, excluding lithography and track.
What does this mean? It means China can now expand mature node capacity far more easily than before, using equipment made domestically within China.

Mature node foundries are booming right now, right? That's thanks to the AI supercycle driving demand for PMICs, power semiconductors, and so on.

Samsung and TSMC shutting down their mature node capacity has also helped a lot.
But here's what I imagine... that China could oversupply mature foundry capacity.

Think about it. If China can be self sufficient in equipment, there's no limit to how far it can expand capacity. Then are companies like TI, with large revenue exposure to China, really safe?

I think it's time to take another look at Western mature foundry companies with a high share of China revenue.

Of course, I'm not saying sell TI right now. I'm just saying we should think about whether it makes sense to hold them for 10 years or more, like Coca Cola.

If you have a different view, please feel free to share it. I’d love to learn.
